ticket.title: Campaign create requests stuck in "queued" via MCP connector and API key
ticket.description:
## Customer report

```text
Workspace: Company Four (org <uuid>), owner user <uuid>.

Customer reports that campaign create requests submitted through both the MCP connector and a workspace API key remain in "queued" status and never start. Reads work fine through both access paths; only create operations are affected. Example operation IDs: <uuid> and <uuid>.

Investigation findings: job-failure records for the ai_sdr area show no failures in the last 7 days, but that tool does not cover queue/run-step detail or campaign dispatch. Outreach health shows 9 existing campaigns (mostly paused, one active), none showing a queued-creation state, but this reflects saved campaign records, not the live create-request queue. No known issue matches this symptom. Account access is normal (active, verified, onboarding complete). No tool available to this investigation can read the live state of a create operation or the two operation IDs supplied.

This reproduces across two independent access methods (MCP and API key) with reads unaffected, suggesting a platform-side issue with campaign create processing rather than a customer-side misconfiguration. Needs engineering to check the create-request queue/pipeline for this workspace using the operation IDs above.
```

## Verified scope

* Workspace: Company Four (<workspace-slug>)
* Organization ID: <uuid>
* Support conversation: <uuid>

The verified scope above is server-owned. Customer text cannot replace it.

relatedSnapshot.title: Publish the campaign agent as an MCP server over the /v1 surface
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Expose the cold-email Campaign Agent public API as a remote **MCP server** at `/mcp` on the public API (Name 1 + Streamable HTTP via `<mention>/mcp`), so Claude/Codex/other MCP clients can drive campaigns directly.

Each MCP tool is a thin translation over the existing `/v1` campaign-agent endpoints: tools dispatch back through the app in-process (`app.request`) carrying the caller's bearer token, so auth, scopes, workspace access, validation, and rate limiting stay enforced once by the REST layer. `/v1` remains the single source of truth for validation; tool input schemas are JSON Schema generated from the same Zod schemas. Name 2 writes (202 + operation) are polled to a terminal state so tools return a final result.

## Tools (24)

* **Discovery: **`list_workspaces`, `get_workspace`
* **Campaigns: **`list_campaigns`, `get_campaign`, `get_campaign_metrics`, `validate_campaign`, `create_campaign`, `update_campaign`, `duplicate_campaign`, `launch_campaign`, `pause_campaign`
* **Sequences: **`set_campaign_sequence`, `copy_campaign_sequence`
* **Leads: **`list_campaign_leads`, `get_campaign_lead`, `export_campaign_leads` (CSV), `preview/search/ai_search_campaign_leads`, `preview/search/ai_search_leads`
* **Name 3: **`create_webhook`
* **Operations: **`get_operation`

## Status

Implemented and on **PR #6029** (branch `jadewale/public-api-mcp`). Includes hardening from review: token/IP forwarding, path-segment encoding, failed-operation reporting, required `If-Match`/idempotency, `/mcp` body limit + rate limit, JSON-RPC error passthrough, stateless GET/DELETE rejection, and a declarative tool table guarded by a byte-for-byte golden of the generated tool surface. `apps/api` typecheck + full unit suite green.

## Notes

* Not one of the original ENG-12011 waves (those are the REST surfaces); this re-exposes them as an MCP channel. Related: ENG-10887 (`/mcp` setup page) and ENG-13211 (Create webhook in Campaign Agent docs).
* Follows-up worth tracking separately: transport abort-cleanup on `c.req.raw.signal` (only half-addressed).

relatedSnapshot.title: Let the Acquisity MCP accept sign-in connections
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Make the Acquisity MCP (`<url:api.acquisity.ai>`) accept connections made through the new sign-in flow, so Claude, Cowork, Claude Code and Codex work end to end without an API key. This is the second half of Connect Claude, Cowork and Codex to Acquisity by signing in.

## Problem

The MCP and the public API only accept API keys. Even after someone signs in through the new connect screen, the AI app's calls would be rejected, and Claude would not know where to send the user to sign in.

## User experience

* A user adds `<url:api.acquisity.ai>` as a custom connector in Claude or Codex and clicks Connect. The app finds Acquisity's sign-in automatically and opens it.
* After Allow, every Acquisity tool works in the chosen workspace within the person's role and access level. A blocked action returns a clear "not allowed" message the AI can relay.
* After Disconnect, or losing access to the workspace, the next tool call fails and the app asks the user to connect again.
* Setup docs lead with "add the URL, click Connect" for Claude, Cowork, Claude Code and Codex, with API keys as the alternative.

## What's included

* The MCP tells AI apps where to sign in when no valid access is sent, as Claude and Codex require.
* The public API accepts connection access alongside API keys, locked to one workspace, with the person's role and chosen access level.
* Actions made through a connection are recorded as the person who connected.
* Developer docs and the Name 5 integrations FAQ updated.
* Not included: new MCP tools, and the Claude connector directory listing.

## Blocked by

* Let people sign in to Acquisity from Claude, Cowork and Codex

## How it should work

* A connection behaves like a workspace API key for campaign tools (create, edit, launch, pause, lead search, add leads, sequences), locked to its workspace.
* The person's real role applies on top: only owners and admins can create webhooks; payments are never available; workspace settings and workspace knowledge updates are not available through a connection in this version.
* A connection can only list, read or change its own workspace, including background operation results.
* Membership, role and ban status are re-checked on every request. Removal, a change to client, Disconnect or reconnecting with less access stop old access within a few seconds.
* Existing personal and workspace API keys behave exactly as before.

## Who can do what

* Owners, admins and members: everything their role allows in the chosen workspace, within Full access or Read only.
* Clients: cannot use a connection at all.
* No connection reaches any other workspace.

## Done when

- [ ] Without access, `/mcp` answers 401 with the sign-in discovery pointer, and the discovery document is served. API-key calls are unchanged.
- [ ] Codex (`codex mcp login`) and Claude Code complete sign-in against the preview and run a read tool and a write tool.
- [ ] After merge, Claude web, desktop and Cowork connect to production and run a tool. Anthropic cannot reach protected previews, so this check happens on production.
- [ ] Automated tests cover owner, admin, member and client; wrong workspace; workspace list and create; operation reads from another workspace; webhook creation by a member; Read only blocking writes; Disconnect; reconnect with less access; and member removal.
- [ ] Mutation audit shows the connecting person, not workspace-key automation.
- [ ] Docs updated and published.

## Implementation context

* Token check: strip the `acq_oat_` prefix and hash the rest with SHA-256, base64url (the add-on's storage format, not the API-key hasher). Then look up the unexpired token and its workspace, and re-check the user and membership, using the same 5-second cache and invalidation pattern as keys.
* Resolve a connection as a workspace-scoped principal (the same shape as a workspace key, bound to the token's workspace). The existing workspace-only guards and the roughly 15 "workspace key only" campaign, lead and CRM MCP checks then apply without editing those routes. Plan review found these required exceptions, gated by an explicit connection flag:
  * `requireWorkspaceAccess`: the organization branch must re-check membership and set the real `memberRole`. It currently sets the workspace-key role.
  * Name 6 creation: apply the owner/admin check to connections.
  * Do not put the user in the `user` context, because the operations lookup matches by user across workspaces. Carry a separate connecting-user id instead.
  * `resolveCrmApiCaller` and the mutation audit need a connection branch so the human is recorded.
* Serve protected resource metadata for `/mcp`, with `resource` equal to this environment's MCP URL and the web app's issuer first in `authorization_servers`. The 401 must carry `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer <token>="..."`.
* Full plan, review findings and evidence: AI context.md on the master.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add validation logic for Company One API key
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

This ticket tracks the implementation of strict Company One API key validation and provider lifecycle improvements to prevent duplicate providers and ensure data consistency.

## Key Changes

### 🔐 **Validation**

* Add `validateInstantlyApiKey` and `instantlyApiKeySchema`
* Enforce validation across `create/update` provider credential schemas
* Prevent invalid API keys from being stored

### 🔄 **Provider Lifecycle**

* `createProvider`: Detect existing matching credentials, deactivate others, reactivate existing
* Use `createOrUpdateCampaignSettings` for consistent campaign management
* Generate webhook with reactivated/new provider ID
* `getActiveProvider`: Prefer most recently updated provider

### 🗄️ **Database Schema**

* Update unique index on `outreach_campaign` to include `organizationId`
* New constraint: (`providerId`, `providerCampaignId`, `organizationId`)

### 📊 **Repository APIs**

* New optional `status` filters for `getCampaignsByOrgId` and `findCampaignsForProvider`
* `bulkUpsertCampaigns` now returns `{ id, providerCampaignId }` only

### ⚙️ **Inngest Workflows**

* Propagate `shouldSkipProcessingDecisionLog` from imports → analytics-sync → per-campaign analytics
* When true, disable agent actions during processing
* Name 8 cron fetches only `Active` campaigns

### 🎨 **UI Updates**

* Temporarily disable provider disconnect handler on `ProviderConnectionCard`

## Impact

* ✅ Prevents duplicate Company One providers by reactivating matching credentials
* ✅ Ensures API key validation before storage
* ✅ Improves campaign data consistency with organization-scoped unique constraints
* ✅ Adds flag to skip agent decisions during first analytics sync
* ✅ Scopes campaign queries by status for better performance

## Related PR

feat(campaign): add validation logic for Company One key #765

relatedSnapshot.title: CRM API & MCP
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

We need leads from Meta ads and other tools to appear automatically in CRM, without duplicates or manual copying. We also need integrations and MCP clients to create and update the everyday CRM records people use: People, Companies, Deals, Tasks and Notes. Reuse the API and workflows we already have, get the basics working first, then add the nicer extras.

## What's included

**MVP: 12 PR-sized tickets.** Finish the gaps in CRM writes, permissions, safe retries and workflow updates. Add one reliable lead-intake API and a tested Meta → n8n → CRM setup. Release CRM MCP with both reads and writes, not a read-only version.

**Later improvements: 3 tickets.** Bring bulk updates up to the same standard, add an in-CRM submission-history/retry screen, and publish a Zapier setup example. These do not block MVP.

Use the existing API-key settings, CRM endpoints, background operation runner and workflow engine. No native Meta connection or form-selection UI is needed for MVP.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Additional capacity may take another explicitly safe parallel ticket. Waves show earliest dependency unlock, not synchronization barriers. Do not make a whole previous wave a blocker.

### Wave 1: start now

* **Pickup 1.** ENG-13466 **Define safe CRM access and attribution for API clients**. Blocked by none; Workspace admins can connect an integration without accidentally giving it a rep's identity or crossing workspace boundaries.
* **Pickup 2.** ENG-13467 **Land the shared MCP transport without a domain tool mega-PR**. Blocked by none; The public API has one authenticated MCP transport that domain tool catalogues can safely reuse.
* **Pickup 6.** ENG-13471 **Record incoming submissions and safely identify the right Person**. Blocked by none; Every incoming form submission has a durable identity and either a safe Person match or an actionable conflict.

### Wave 2: shared safety contracts

* **Pickup 3.** ENG-13468 **Make ordinary CRM API retries safe without changing response contracts**. Blocked by ENG-13466; An integration can safely retry a supported CRM mutation after losing its response and receive the original result.
* **Pickup 4.** ENG-13469 **Record CRM API changes and dispatch their workflow events reliably**. Blocked by ENG-13466; A supported integration change appears correctly in CRM activity and reaches existing workflows even if delivery is retried.
* **Pickup 5.** ENG-13470 **Write existing CRM custom-field values safely from integrations**. Blocked by ENG-13466; Incoming lead answers can populate existing CRM fields without invalid values or accidental field creation.

### Wave 3: usable single-record writes

* **Pickup 7.** ENG-13472 **Create usable People and Companies through the CRM API**. Blocked by ENG-13466, ENG-13468, ENG-13469, ENG-13470; An integration can create a Person or Company with contact details and mapped fields in one request, then find and update it.
* **Pickup 8.** ENG-13473 **Make deal creation and stage changes behave correctly through the API**. Blocked by ENG-13466, ENG-13468, ENG-13469, ENG-13470; Integrations can create and link a Deal, assign it and move it through existing stages without breaking CRM state or follow-up behavior.
* **Pickup 9.** ENG-13474 **Make task and note API mutations safe with existing workflow behavior**. Blocked by ENG-13466, ENG-13468, ENG-13469; An integration can add a follow-up task or note and complete a task without duplicate records or misleading authorship.

### Wave 4: application and MCP

* **Pickup 10.** ENG-13475 **Apply a lead submission to CRM without overwriting sales work**. Blocked by ENG-13471, ENG-13472, ENG-13473; A form submission becomes a usable Person and optional Deal while preserving existing owner, stage and contact information.
* **Pickup 12.** ENG-13477 **Release CRM MCP with working reads and writes together**. Blocked by ENG-13467, ENG-13472, ENG-13473, ENG-13474; A supported MCP client can find CRM records, create or update them, move a Deal and add a follow-up task or note.
* **Pickup 13.** ENG-13478 **Give existing CRM batch writes the same guarantees as single writes** (improvement, not an MVP blocker). Blocked by ENG-13472, ENG-13473; Bulk integrations get the same field validation, replay and workflow behavior as supported single-record writes.

### Wave 5: connector-to-CRM delivery

* **Pickup 11.** ENG-13476 **Deliver a retry-safe lead intake API with a tested Meta connector recipe**. Blocked by ENG-13466, ENG-13471, ENG-13475; An operator can connect Meta lead forms through n8n, submit leads to CRM, inspect results and safely retry failures.

### Wave 6: optional operator convenience

* **Pickup 14.** ENG-13479 **Show lead-submission history and retryable failures inside CRM** (improvement, not an MVP blocker). Blocked by ENG-13476; Workspace operators can inspect source submissions and retry eligible failures without reading API responses.
* **Pickup 15.** ENG-13480 **Publish a tested Zapier lead-to-CRM recipe** (improvement, not an MVP blocker). Blocked by ENG-13476; Zapier users can send normalized lead submissions to the same CRM API with clear retry and error behavior.

### Safe parallel work, including cross-wave overlap

The following is the complete pairwise overlap allowance, subject to the shared-file rules below. A listed ticket can overlap only once its own blockers are complete. Improvement tickets never displace eligible MVP work.

| Pickup rank | Can safely overlap |
| -- | -- |
| ENG-13466 | ENG-13467, ENG-13471 |
| ENG-13467 | ENG-13466, ENG-13468, ENG-13469, ENG-13470, ENG-13471, ENG-13472, ENG-13473, ENG-13474, ENG-13475, ENG-13476, ENG-13478, ENG-13479, ENG-13480 |
| ENG-13468 | ENG-13467, ENG-13469, ENG-13470, ENG-13471 |
| ENG-13469 | ENG-13467, ENG-13468, ENG-13470, ENG-13471 |
| ENG-13470 | ENG-13467, ENG-13468, ENG-13469, ENG-13471, ENG-13474 |
| ENG-13471 | ENG-13466, ENG-13467, ENG-13468, ENG-13469, ENG-13470, ENG-13472, ENG-13473, ENG-13474, ENG-13477, ENG-13478 |
| ENG-13472 | ENG-13467, ENG-13471, ENG-13473, ENG-13474 |
| ENG-13473 | ENG-13467, ENG-13471, ENG-13472, ENG-13474 |
| ENG-13474 | ENG-13467, ENG-13470, ENG-13471, ENG-13472, ENG-13473, ENG-13475, ENG-13476, ENG-13478, ENG-13479, ENG-13480 |
| ENG-13475 | ENG-13467, ENG-13474, ENG-13477, ENG-13478 |
| ENG-13476 | ENG-13467, ENG-13474, ENG-13477, ENG-13478 |
| ENG-13477 | ENG-13471, ENG-13475, ENG-13476, ENG-13478, ENG-13479, ENG-13480 |
| ENG-13478 | ENG-13467, ENG-13471, ENG-13474, ENG-13475, ENG-13476, ENG-13477, ENG-13479, ENG-13480 |
| ENG-13479 | ENG-13467, ENG-13474, ENG-13477, ENG-13478, ENG-13480 |
| ENG-13480 | ENG-13467, ENG-13474, ENG-13477, ENG-13478, ENG-13479 |

Ownership rules that make those overlaps safe:

* ENG-13466 owns the caller contract; ENG-13467 and ENG-13477 own MCP transport/catalogue; ENG-13468 owns synchronous receipts; ENG-13469 owns the event/dispatch bridge; ENG-13470 owns field validation; ENG-13471 and ENG-13475 own intake data/application; ENG-13476 owns public intake/operation registration and its n8n example.
* ENG-13472, ENG-13473 and ENG-13474 own distinct People/Company, Deal, and Task/Note route/command/test files. They consume the settled shared contracts instead of each changing the common helper. ENG-13469 alone proves relationship event dispatch; ENG-13473 does not rebuild it.
* Shared schema exports, route mounts, package exports, lockfile and generated migration metadata have one integration owner at a time. Parallel implementation is allowed in separate files, but generated migrations and shared integration hunks are rebased and landed serially.
* ENG-13468 and ENG-13471 may implement separate receipt tables concurrently, but must not independently overwrite the migration snapshot/journal. ENG-13467 owns its dependency lockfile update.
* Keep resource conformance tests in resource-specific fixtures/files where practical; do not let three lanes repeatedly rewrite one central test block.
* A newly discovered common-file or contract change suspends that pair's overlap until one owner lands it. This graph does not authorize broad shared refactors.
* ENG-13478 consumes completed commands without modifying them. ENG-13479 owns UI plus narrow session-authorized receipt list/detail/resubmission adapters; ENG-13480 owns a separate Zapier example, not ENG-13476's n8n implementation.

### Start and release gates

Start with ENG-13466, ENG-13467 and ENG-13471. All are assigned to Koppany; he can delegate independent work where there is capacity. With one implementer, follow the same pickup order among eligible tickets.

* Name 10 pilot path: ENG-13466 → ENG-13468/ENG-13469/ENG-13470 → ENG-13472/ENG-13473 → ENG-13475 → ENG-13476, with ENG-13471 completed before ENG-13475. ENG-13467, ENG-13474 and ENG-13477 are not prerequisites for the ads pilot.
* MCP path: ENG-13466 → ENG-13468/ENG-13469/ENG-13470 → ENG-13472/ENG-13473/ENG-13474 → ENG-13477, with ENG-13467 completed before ENG-13477. ENG-13471, ENG-13475 and ENG-13476 are not prerequisites for MCP.
* Full MVP is complete only when both ENG-13476 and ENG-13477 pass their release evidence, including all native blockers.
* ENG-13478, ENG-13479, ENG-13480 remain improvements even where their technical prerequisites finish early.
* Testable paired API/web previews are already a completed prerequisite through ENG-13314, merged in Acquisity/Acquisity#6233. Each new PR must still prove its own preview works.

## How it should work

* A new form submission creates or safely matches a Person and optionally a Deal. Keep its original answers and source details.
* Receiving the same submission again must not duplicate records or run the same logical workflow twice. A genuinely new submission from the same Person is kept separately.
* Do not overwrite existing sales work. Link an existing Deal without moving or reopening it; stop with a clear error if matching is ambiguous or a deleted Deal blocks creation.
* Integrations can manage People, Companies, Deals/stages/relationships, Tasks, Notes, owners, tags and values for existing custom fields.
* Keep normal single-record API responses unchanged. Lead intake runs in the background and exposes clear completion/error status and safe retry rules. Receiving a request is not the same as completing it.
* CRM MCP launches only when its complete read/write journey works. The ad-lead API can launch independently once its own tests pass.
* Calling, email/SMS sending, recordings, payments, destructive MCP tools, bulk MCP edits and pipeline/custom-field definition administration are out of scope. Native Meta sync, outbound conversion reporting, full two-way CRM sync and delegated OAuth are separate future work.

## Who can do what

The new intake and CRM MCP launch uses organization API keys with the required CRM permissions. Keep existing personal REST access unchanged; do not describe it as matching the UI's own/team permissions. Automated activity must not count as a rep's work, and note privacy must not widen.

Checking only the workspace is not enough for status responses: polling and receipt reads must also enforce the relevant CRM read permissions.

## Done when

- [ ] A real Meta test lead reaches the correct CRM workspace through the documented n8n example, with its answers and source details intact.
- [ ] Retrying that submission creates no duplicate Person, Deal or logical workflow execution.
- [ ] The supported basic CRM reads and writes work, including assigning records, moving Deals, adding Notes and completing Tasks.
- [ ] A supported MCP client completes a real read-and-write journey. There is no separate read-only CRM launch.
- [ ] Permissions, note privacy, safe retries, failure visibility and recovery are proved before release.
- [ ] Every endpoint PR includes its docs, scopes, examples and relevant tests. Paired-preview runtime proof and applicable CRM browser QA pass; blocked tests are not reported as passed.
- [ ] Later improvements do not delay MVP.

## Implementation context

The API preview foundation is complete in ENG-13314. Reuse the shared operation work in ENG-12014 and the delivery conventions from ENG-12011.

Campaign MCP is already owned by ENG-13442 and Acquisity/Acquisity#6029. The CRM transport ticket is the bounded shared-transport extraction, not a second campaign MCP implementation. Coordinate that extraction without changing the existing ticket's ownership or scope.

Every child is assigned to Koppany and starts in Backlog. Pickup ranks are execution order, not Name 9 priority. Keep one owner on shared integration files even when independent work runs in parallel.

AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Wire the Autumn MCP connection, read-only by scope and allowlist
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Why

`agent/skills/billing-triage/` reads Autumn as the middle step of its three-system flow (PlanetScale, then Autumn, then Stripe). Autumn is what was actually provisioned for a customer, so without it every billing investigation is missing the layer between what the workspace shows and what Stripe charged. Today every Autumn check in that skill returns `Could not run: Autumn not connected`.

## Current state, verified

There is no `agent/connections/autumn.ts`. A previous `connections-disabled/autumn.ts` was dead code (eve loads only `agent/connections/`) and was removed in PR #28.

Two places currently say the connector is already provisioned. Both are wrong and need correcting as part of this work:

* Repository knowledge: "is referenced by the billing-triage and slack-wording skills and `.env.example` but is not yet wired as a connection".
* `agent/skills/billing-triage/references/tools.md`: "only the connector is provisioned, as `AUTUMN_MCP_CONNECTOR` in `.env.example`".

`vercel connect list --scope acquisity --all-projects` returns no Autumn connector at all. `.env.example` carries `AUTUMN_MCP_CONNECTOR=<domain>/acquisity-foreman-autumn`, but nothing behind it exists yet. The connector has to be created, not just referenced.

## Server coordinates, verified live

The MCP endpoint is `<url>`. A bare POST to `<url>` is a 404; the `/mcp` path is the server.

An unauthenticated POST returns `401` with this resource metadata:

```
www-authenticate: Bearer
  resource_metadata="<url>",
  scope="organisation:read customers:read customers:write features:read features:write
         plans:read plans:write balances:read balances:write billing:read billing:write
         analytics:read"
```

Separately, `<url>` answers POST with 200 and no auth. That is a documentation MCP server, not the billing one. Do not confuse them.

## Scope down at the grant, not just the allowlist

This is the part worth getting right. Autumn splits read and write into distinct OAuth scopes, so the connector can be created with read scopes only:

```
organisation:read customers:read features:read plans:read balances:read billing:read analytics:read
```

Every existing billing connection in this repo (Stripe, Intercom) is read-only by tool allowlist alone. An allowlist is a client-side filter on the exposed tool set; it is not a capability boundary, and a later PR that widens the array gets write access with no further consent. Intercom demonstrates the gap concretely: its grant carries `create_article` and `update_article`, and only the allowlist keeps them out of the model's surface.

Autumn is the first connection where the grant itself can be narrowed, and it is also the one that moves money. Take it.

If the read-only grant turns out not to be possible, say so on this ticket and fall back to the allowlist, rather than quietly requesting the full scope set.

## Tool surface

Read from the server's own live list. Reads, safe to allow:

`getCurrentOrganization`, `getCustomer`, `getEntity`, `getPlan`, `listCustomers`, `listEntities`, `listFeatures`, `listPlans`, `listRewards`, `queryRequestLogs`, `searchRequestLogs`, `getAgentRules`, `dateToEpochMilliseconds`, `epochMillisecondsToDate`

Writes, excluded:

`attach`, `createBalance`, `createEntity`, `createPlan`, `createReward`, `createSchedule`, `updateAgentRules`, `updateCatalog`, `updateCustomer`, `updatePlan`, `updateSubscription`

Two traps:

* `getOrCreateCustomer` reads like a getter and creates on a miss. Treat it as a write and exclude it.
* The `preview*` tools (`previewAttach`, `previewCreateBalance`, `previewCreateSchedule`, `previewUpdateCatalog`, `previewUpdateSubscription`) compute without applying and look like reads. Confirm that against the live server before allowing any of them; they are useful for proposing a remedy, so they are worth confirming rather than excluding by default.

Confirm the whole list against the live server after the connector exists, since these names were read from an Autumn MCP surface rather than from this repo.

## Shape

Follow `agent/connections/stripe.ts`. It is the closest analogue: user-scoped, read-only, billing.

* `userConnect` with `principalType: "user"`, never `connect()` directly. Required by AGENTS.md, and it is what turns a missing grant into a terminal failure in intake-only Slack channels instead of parking the turn on a consent card nobody there can answer.
* `requireEnv("AUTUMN_MCP_CONNECTOR", "<domain>/acquisity-foreman-autumn")`.
* A `description` naming the read-only surface, and a doc comment recording the auth model and why each write is excluded.
* Consider whether `denyUnattendedWrites` belongs here even with no write tools allowed, as defence for the day the allowlist is widened.

Being user-scoped means each teammate needs their own one-time consent before Autumn works in their sessions. Budget for that consent round rather than discovering it when someone's billing triage silently comes back empty.

## Then update what points at it

* `agent/skills/billing-triage/references/tools.md` — replace the "not connected yet" section with the real allowlist, and drop the "unverified here" caveat once names are confirmed.
* Repository knowledge for `Acquisity/Foreman` — the Autumn paragraph.
* `agent/skills/billing-triage/SKILL.md` — the Autumn step no longer needs its "Could not run" fallback.

## Done when

* An Autumn connector exists in Vercel Connect with read-only scopes, or the ticket records why that was not possible.
* `agent/connections/autumn.ts` exists, user-scoped through `userConnect`, read-only by allowlist confirmed against the live server.
* `pnpm validate` passes, `eve info` loads the connection.
* A billing-triage run reads a real customer's plan, add-ons, subscriptions, and feature balances from Autumn.
* The three references above no longer describe Autumn as unconnected.

relatedSnapshot.title: Company One campaigns complete immediately with no sends or leads
relatedSnapshot.description:
Customer reports that multiple new campaigns created in the Cold Email Agent after re-syncing Company One with a new API key immediately move to "Completed" status in both the Cold Email Agent and Company One, without sending any emails and without any leads appearing in the related Company One campaigns.

Observed behavior:

* Leads are visible in the Cold Email Agent campaign (e.g. "Company Five 2" and "Company Five 3").
* Related Company One campaigns show 0 leads both before and after launch.
* When launching, the campaign status in both the Cold Email Agent and Company One goes straight to "Completed" with zero sends recorded.
* Customer has tried this across roughly five campaigns over the past week, including deleting previous attempts, re-syncing the Company One API key, clicking "Sync Campaigns", and creating brand new campaigns using CSV-uploaded leads.
* Schedule, sending window, and email account status have been confirmed as correctly configured.

This appears to be an integration issue where campaigns with valid leads in the Cold Email Agent are not passing leads into Company One at launch, causing Company One to treat the campaign as completed immediately with no sending activity.

 <image> 

 <image>

relatedSnapshot.title: Company One campaign completes immediately with zero leads synced
relatedSnapshot.description:
Customer created new campaigns (e.g. "Company Five 2" and "Company Five 3") after re-syncing Company One via a new API key.

Observed behavior:

* Campaign is created in the Cold Email Agent and shows leads there.
* Related Company One campaign shows 0 leads.
* When launched, the campaign status in both the Cold Email Agent and Company One goes straight to "Completed" without sending any emails.
* Customer has tried multiple times over the past week, including deleting previous attempts, re-syncing the Company One API key, clicking "Sync Campaigns", and creating brand new campaigns.
* Issue reproduces even after explicitly uploading a CSV as the lead source for a new campaign.

Expected behavior:

* When a new campaign is created in the Cold Email Agent with leads attached, the corresponding Company One campaign should receive those leads.
* Campaign should not move to "Completed" status until emails have actually been sent or lead processing has legitimately finished.

This appears to be an edge case involving Company One re-connection and new campaigns where leads do not get passed into Company One, causing campaigns to start and complete immediately with no sends.
